meta.description: Search NCBI databases using Biopython Bio.Entrez (ESearch, EInfo, ESpell), including cross-database counts via an ESearch loop over a disclosed 10-of-38 curated database subset, with a verified widen-to-all-databases escape hatch (EGQuery is broken on current Biopython/NCBI). Use when finding records by keyword, building reproducible field-qualified queries, navigating the Entrez Query Translator, exploiting the history server for large result sets, handling retmax caps, or interpreting weekly index lag. Covers PubMed, Nucleotide, Protein, Gene, SRA, GEO, Assembly, Taxonomy, ClinVar, dbSNP.

scientific_integrity.detail: All counts, UIDs, field lists, database counts, and the 38-database EInfo figure across all 9 executed inputs came from live NCBI E-utilities calls made independently in this re-audit (not reused from the fix log or prior reports); none fabricated.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure database-search tooling; no output makes diagnostic, prescriptive, or treatment claims about an individual.

methodological_ground.detail: No correlation/causation conflation. The second fix pass's disclosure of CURATED_DBS's 10/38 scope (rather than implying exhaustive coverage) and its dropping of the unverifiable 'Tue/Fri' indexer claim in favor of the supported 'nightly' claim are both methodologically sound choices, independently confirmed in this audit.

code_usability.detail: All 9 inputs executed to completion with real, checked output; no syntax errors, no missing dependencies. Fenced code blocks were extracted programmatically from the shipped SKILL.md in the fix worktree, not hand-copied, and ran unmodified.

functional_suitability.note: The one remaining pre-fix gap (CURATED_DBS decision-table row implying exhaustive coverage) is now closed: reworded to name the 10 curated databases, with a disclosure paragraph and a widen-to-all-databases snippet independently verified in this audit to run clean across all 38 live databases, not just the fixer's 2-db spot check.

reliability.note: Failure Modes and Common Errors tables remain thorough and re-verified live (retmax cap, WebEnv expiration body, RuntimeError-not-fabrication on <ERROR> bodies). Unchanged from the prior re-audit; no new reliability gap found.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md net +5 lines this pass (334 -> 339); still a single flat file with no references/ split despite the redundancy pass. usage-guide.md shrank (74 -> 65) by removing genuinely duplicated content, a real but small efficiency gain.

agent_usability.note: The CURATED_DBS coverage gap that previously cost a point here (undisclosed scope, an error-prevention miss) is fixed and disclosed as a pitfall. The Failure Modes internal contradiction (indexer 'Tue/Fri' vs 'nightly') found and resolved during this fix pass removes a real consistency defect; confirmed absent in this audit.

human_usability.note: Unchanged; MARCH1 worked example still matches live reality, natural trigger language retained.

security.note: New term-validation paragraph after Required Setup, independently tested in this audit: Bio.Entrez has no shell/eval call sites, builds requests via urllib.parse (percent-encoding), and a live call with a shell-metacharacter-laden term transmitted safely with no unescaped metacharacters. Guidance is prose-only (no runnable sanitization helper), so not full marks.

maintainability.note: Redundancy pass collapsed 4 duplicated Failure Modes entries to one-line pointers and removed usage-guide.md's entire Tips section (content verified to have migrated to SKILL.md, not lost -- see eval_viewer). This reduces future drift risk (single source of truth) but references/ modularity split is still absent.

agent_specific.note: Trigger description now names the disclosed 10/38 scope accurately. Progressive disclosure (8.2) remains the one held-back point: examples/ are cross-linked but no references/ split exists despite the file's complexity.

inputs.label: NEW: term-validation / injection-safety claim in the new Required-Setup paragraph, tested rather than trusted
inputs.note: executed: true. Static scan of Bio/Entrez/__init__.py and Parser.py found no os.system/subprocess/eval/exec/shell=True call sites; confirmed request construction goes through urllib.parse (percent-encoding). A live ESearch call with a term containing shell metacharacters and quotes (';', backtick, '$()', '&&', quotes) transmitted with every metacharacter percent-encoded and returned a normal Count=0 with no crash or server-side execution. SKILL.md's claim ('no shell/eval injection risk') holds under direct test, not just inspection.

assertions.text: Bio.Entrez source contains no shell/eval call sites (os.system, subprocess, eval, exec, shell=True)
Bio.Entrez builds request query strings via urllib.parse, not raw string interpolation
A term with shell metacharacters is fully percent-encoded before transmission
assertions.note: None of ; ` $ | & survived unescaped in the encoded form.

assertions.text: A live call with the malicious-looking term completes normally with no crash or execution
assertions.note: Count=0 returned; QueryTranslation shows the term parsed as ordinary search terms, not executed.

key_strengths: The CURATED_DBS exhaustiveness defect that held the prior re-audit below Production Ready (Layer-2 specialized average 47.3 against a 48 floor) is genuinely fixed: the decision table now names the 10-db scope, a disclosure paragraph states the 10/38 fraction, and the widen-to-all-databases escape hatch was independently run in this audit across the FULL 38-database list (38/38 succeeded, 0 errors) -- not just the fixer's 2-db spot check.

The internal contradiction the fixer caught while collapsing Failure Modes (indexer 'batch Tue/Fri primary' vs 'runs nightly') is confirmed gone from both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md; the surviving 'nightly' claim is the one with documentation support.

The new term-validation paragraph's security claim ('no shell/eval injection risk') was tested, not trusted: source inspection plus a live call with a shell-metacharacter-laden term confirmed percent-encoding and no server-side execution.
The redundancy pass's claimed content migrations (PMC-subset fact, 4 collapsed Failure Modes entries) were spot-checked in this audit and confirmed present in SKILL.md, not lost.

Both pre-fix P1 code-crash defects (EGQuery AttributeError, EInfo DbInfo dict-indexing) remain durably fixed across all inputs in this audit, including databases and terms never touched by either fixer.

recommendations.title: No progressive disclosure despite SKILL.md growing longer across two fix passes
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md is now 339 lines (up from ~300 pre-fix), still a single flat file with all failure-mode and field tables inline. Both fix passes declined the references/ split as out of scope for FIX_BRIEF.md's restructuring limit.
recommendations.root_cause: Restructuring beyond the redundancy rule was explicitly out of scope for both fix passes; a reasonable call given the mandate, but the underlying static-score gap remains.
recommendations.fix: In a future pass with restructuring scope, split the field-qualified-pattern tables and Failure Modes/Common Errors tables into a references/ file.

recommendations.title: Term-validation guidance is prose-only, no runnable helper
recommendations.problem: The new paragraph after Required Setup correctly explains that terms are URL-encoded (verified true in this audit), but gives no code example for the length/count sanity-check it recommends before large batch loops.
recommendations.root_cause: The finding was addressed with documentation only, matching its P2 priority from the fix log.
recommendations.fix: Add a 3-line helper function (e.g. warn if len(term) > N or term.count(' OR ') > M) alongside the existing EPost-chunking pointer.
